title: Generating the symmetric group by three prefix reversals: the case m = n - 2 of the three-prefix-reversal classification (printed as Theorem 4)
author: Sa\'ul A. Blanco, Mikhail P. Golubyatnikov, Elena V. Konstantinova, Natalia V. Maslova, Luka A. Nikiforov
work: Generating the symmetric group by three prefix reversals
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 4 (source0.tex lines 663--665, source label thm:n-2), the case m = n - 2 of the classification of triples of prefix reversals generating the symmetric group: for H generated by r_n, r_{n-2} and r_k with 2 <= k < n-2 and n >= 5, H is the full symmetric group if and only if n and k have different parities. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 667--837 (171 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral) and with the context the proof uses. The proof is a genuine research argument: after reducing k in {2,3} to the two earlier theorems, it exhibits an explicit (n-2)-cycle as a product of two prefix reversals, multiplies it by the third generator, and tracks the resulting permutation through long chains of residues modulo 2m to read off a transposition of two adjacent entries of that cycle, which the article's classical n-cycle-and-transposition lemma turns into generation; in the other parity-compatible case it conjugates the transposition (1 2) by powers of the (n-2)-cycle to produce all transpositions between odd and even positions, that is, the Coxeter generators, and it closes the reverse implication with the parity obstruction from the introduction. The substantive steps are the residue-chain computations, the identification of the induced transposition and the Coxeter-generator argument; none of them is an unpacking of definitions. H3: a complete original research-paper proof of a main case of the paper's classification, with every hypothesis and every invoked observation retained.
